advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make backfill() measure the tree at each sha (e.g. `git archive`/`git worktree add` into a temp dir and pass that path to measure_tree) instead of always passing repo_root.
evidence: Docstring line 3-5: 'measures cyclomatic complexity and the clone count of the source tree at that commit'
No `git checkout`, `git archive`, `git worktree`, or per-sha tree extraction exists anywhere in the file (only `_commit_date` reads `%cI` for the sha; the sha is otherwise unused for measurement).
measure_tree's own docstring (line 28-34) describes measuring the tree 'at tree_path', but backfill passes repo_root, not a commit-specific path.
advisory.finding: backfill() measures the current working tree for every commit instead of the tree at each sampled sha: it calls measure_tree(repo_root) with a fixed repo_root and never checks out / archives the commit. So all snapshots record identical complexity/clone_count (only the timestamp differs), defeating the script's stated goal of a real historical trend.
scenarios: Running the backfill over N historical commits produces N snapshots that all carry the same complexity/clone_count taken from HEAD/working state, tagged with different commit dates.
advisory.suggested_fix: For each sha, extract the tree at that commit into a temp dir (e.g. `git -C repo_root worktree add --detach <tmp> <sha>` or `git archive <sha> | tar -x -C <tmp>`) and call measure_tree(<tmp>), cleaning up afterward.

The stubs even accept a `tree` arg but assert nothing about which path is passed.
merged_from: No test exercises the real measurement code (`measure_tree`, `_measure_complexity`, `_measure_clone_count`); every test monkeypatches `measure_tree` to a constant, so the lizard row-parsing, jscpd JSON `statistics.total.clones` extraction, return-code handling, and the exception/None-collapse logic are entirely untested and a regression in any of them would ship silently.
scenarios: A regression where every commit is measured identically (the current behavior) passes all tests.

advisory.finding: The central contract 'measure the tree AT the sampled commit' is not pinned by any test: `backfill` calls `measure_tree(repo_root)` (the current working tree, no checkout of `sha`), and because the stub ignores its argument and returns a constant, no test asserts what tree/path measure_tree receives per commit — so the tests cannot detect that the wrong (current) tree is measured for every historical commit.
advisory.suggested_fix: Have the stub record the `tree` argument per call and assert it reflects each commit's checked-out content, or return content-dependent values and assert distinct snapshots per commit.
